content.title: Santa Clara coach unsuccessfully called for timeout before Kentucky’s buzzer-beater
content.text: The final seconds of regulation between seventh-seeded Kentucky and 10th-seeded Santa Clara in the first round of the NCAA Tournament will be played over and over as a signature March Madness moment. Kentucky ended up winning 89-84 in overtime. But look closer.Santa Clara’s Allen Graves hit what appeared to be the game-winning 3 to push the Broncos ahead 73-70 with two seconds remaining. But in a flash, Kentucky’s Otega Oweh raced down the floor and banked in a prayer to tie the score at 73, forcing overtime.In between, Santa Clara coach Herb Sendek signaled to the referee for a timeout to set his defense just a few beats after Graves buried the go-ahead shot. The referee was already sprinting the other way without a second look back at the 63-year-old head coach.No timeout was granted, and Oweh sprinted unimpeded to force extra basketball. 🚨 Close-up shows Herb Sendek trying to call timeout right before Otega Oweh’s game-tying 3 for Kentucky Wildcats 😳🏀 A split-second moment that changed everything. pic.twitter.com/86UbvVDC8Q — Sports Insider (@sportssiinsider) March 20, 2026“I unequivocally called timeout,” Sendek said postgame. “But they didn’t grant it. I mean, I think the video evidence is clear. And anybody is able to pull it up. Top League Content “It’s a likely response after Allen hits the 3 that the coach would be calling timeout to set the defense, which I tried to do, and I was successful in doing, other than it wasn’t acknowledged.”Coaches are allowed to call a timeout on dead balls, which was the case before Kentucky inbounded the ball. Had Sendek been granted his timeout, he could have set a better defensive lineup on the floor or instructed his team to foul up 3, sending Kentucky to the line with a maximum of 2 points available.Your browser does not support the video tag.0:00 / 0:00Now that question will weigh heavily on Santa Clara’s first tournament appearance since 1996, and a season in which the Broncos went 26-9 and made the WCC championship game for the first time since 2007.What if?In the chaos, not even his own players had enough time to process that Sendek might want a timeout to configure a plan for the final two perilous seconds.“Honestly, there was just so much going on in that moment,” senior forward Elijah Mahi said.Go-ahead shot already buried against a blue blood. Two seconds away. One heave and a prayer, and one referee looking in the other direction as Santa Clara saw its win vanish. In the five-minute overtime, the gusto had been taken from the Broncos’ stride, and Kentucky overmatched them.But what if Sendek had just gotten that timeout?“It was a really euphoric high,” he said, “followed by a tough one to swallow.” Connections: Sports EditionSpot the pattern.
